title: Retry coordination, request redispatch, and observability runbook for Hosted API 5xx/timeouts
creator: Nadia Park
description:
Summary: Multiple customers reported elevated 5xx spikes and long tail timeouts during tenant burst events. Investigation shows a combination of (1) request fanout into edge proxy pools, (2) aggressive client SDK retries without global dedup/hedging awareness, and (3) uneven KV-cache eviction that amplified backend latency. This ticket defines a short-term production-safe fix (redispatch + staged backoff), a telemetry/alerting surface to detect amplification, and a runbook for Customer Success/Support for ongoing escalations across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Observed behavior:
- Surface: Hosted API returning intermittent 500/502/504 and >5s end-to-end latencies for a subset of tenants during sudden surge (spikes correlate to tenant onboarding flows).
- Amplification: SDK retries + proxy-level fanout created duplicate in-flight requests that overwhelmed model worker queues and caused KV-cache churn.
- Secondary effects: Downstream autoscaling reacted slowly; Dedicated pools showed similar symptoms but were constrained by pinned capacity; Private installs had some mitigations via local network settings but lacked unified telemetry.

Goals:
1) Implement a minimal redispatch shim at the edge to avoid duplicate backend execution when retries happen within a short window.
2) Coordinate SDK retry semantics with server-side idempotency keys and tenant-scoped request cooling.
3) Add signals/alerts (dashboard and paging) for retry amplification, KV-cache evictions per tenant, and proxy fanout ratios.
4) Produce an operational runbook for Support/SEs to triage and remediate customer escalations quickly.

Proposed short-term fixes (safe for production rollout):
- Edge Redispatch Guard: Add a 200ms window at the edge layer keyed by request idempotency (x-rw-request-id) to dedupe duplicate inflight requests and return a shared response stream where possible. Fallback: if responses diverge, mark audit and fall through to normal path.
- Tenant Cooling: Implement per-tenant token bucket at ingress that emits a slowpath header when saturated so downstream throttlers can prioritize.
- Retry Coordination Header: Add x-rw-retry-count and x-rw-retry-timestamp to surface SDK retries; update SDKs to send these.
- Observability: New Grafana panels for "retry amplification ratio" (retries/unique requests), per-tenant KV-cache eviction rate, and edge fanout factor. Create alert when amplification ratio > 1.5 for >2m.

Risk and trade-offs:
- Dedup window may increase perceived tail latency for the first request if shared-waiting used; tradeoff mitigated by conservative 200ms default and ability to disable per-tenant.
- Shared-response approach adds complexity for streaming requests; initial rollout will only dedupe non-streaming generation calls.
- SDK changes require coordinated rollout; server-side headers are defensive and will work without immediate SDK updates but provide better telemetry once adopted.

Scope differences by deployment mode:
- Hosted: Full feature set (redispatch guard + telemetry + tenant cooling) can be deployed quickly; priority for customers currently escalated.
- Dedicated: Recommend configuration bundle (edge redispatch + tenant cooling) shipped as upgrade flag; operators may opt-in for shared response.
- Private: Provide guidance and patch that mirrors edge redispatch behavior; limited with private networking and KMS differences, so telemetry integration will be via exported metrics endpoints.

Acceptance criteria:
- Edge dedupe implemented behind feature flag and exercised against synthetic tenant surge tests with end-to-end traffic replay.
- Observability panels and alerts deployed to production for a 2-week burn with noise tuning.
- SDKs emit retry headers in at least 2 language SDKs and docs updated.
- Runbook published and a DR drill executed with Support within 7 days of rollout.

Links to artifacts: GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge/pull/4287 (WIP), Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Retry+Coordination+and+Redispatch, Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/hosted/retry-amplification

Next steps:
- Engineering: land redispatch guard behind feature flag and integration test harness (ETA 5 days).
- Observability: add metrics and alert rules (ETA 3 days).
- SDK/Docs: update two main SDKs and publish migration note (ETA 10 days).
- Support: runbook draft and tabletop for escalations (owner: CS lead).
